title: Native Multi-Dimensional Subquadratic Operators via Input Dependent Long Convolutions
claim: Prior global operators are either quadratic or inherently 1D; ours is natively multi-dimensional and subquadratic, scaling to million-token inputs.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right: three operator diagrams on one image, then a log-scale plot
description: The figure has two parts. On the left, three side-by-side panels show the same cartoon hyena image cut into a 5x5 grid of patches. Each panel is titled Attention, Mamba or HyenaND (Ours). A central eye patch is highlighted, and green arrows show how information flows to it. In Attention, arrows from every patch point inward, labeled O(L^2). In Mamba, arrows follow a 1D raster or zigzag scan order, with dashed green lines marking the scan path, labeled O(L). In HyenaND, arrows from every patch point inward as in Attention, labeled O(L log L). On the right, a log-log line plot shows forward time in ms against sequence length from 4K to 1M. The lines are HyenaND in red, Attention in blue and Mamba in green. Attention rises steeply, and a 339x gap is annotated at 1M. Mamba shows OOM at 1M.
caption: (Left): Complexity of global multi-dimensional operators by token count L. Attention is natively multi-dimensional but scales quadratically. Mamba is subquadratic but inherently 1D, requiring ad-hoc 1D scan orders to process multi-dimensional data. HyenaND (ours) is global, natively multi-dimensional and subquadratic. (Right): Forward-pass time vs. sequence length using flash-attention, the official mamba chunk scan combined Mamba2 kernel and nSubQ; HyenaND scales gracefully to million-token sequences while attention collapses at long contexts.
abstract: Subquadratic alternatives to attention require compromises when applied to multi-dimensional data: standard convolutions lack global receptive fields and input dependency, while recurrent models require rasterizing data such as images, volumes, and partial differential equation (PDE) into an ad-hoc $1\rm D$ scan order that violates their spatial structure. We introduce \textit{HyenaND}, a subquadratic, global, input-dependent operator that acts directly on the native geometry of multidimensional data through convolutions with implicitly parametrized global, input-dependent multi-dimensional convolutional kernels. Our CUDA implementation, \texttt{nSubQ}, fuses the FFT-convolution path to turn HyenaND's $\mathcal{O}(L \log L)$ scaling into wall-clock speedups. Across long-context genomics, computer vision, medical imaging, and PDE modeling, pure HyenaND stacks match the accuracy of strong attention baselines, while hybrid configurations that interleave HyenaND and attention layers outperform both pure attention and strong recurrence-based hybrids.
